answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. It survives because reputation is spent fast and earned slowly, so any alias that ever cheats loses value that is expensive to replace. The mechanism therefore aligns self-interest with network health: an attacker gains most by behaving honestly, because that is the only move that scales. Consider a velvet as the anchor of the cost.
